name: HNW Investment Portfolio Review
description: A Wealth Advisor (PER-057) conducts a periodic MiFID II COBS 9A suitability review for an HNW Client (PER-004), reassesses the client's risk profile and investment objectives, presents updated portfolio performance and proposed rebalancing recommendations, obtains the client's instructions, executes the approved rebalancing trades via the custody platform, and issues a compliant suitability report. The journey spans CAP-006 (Wealth Management — primary capability), CAP-005 (Compliance — MiFID II suitability record and Consumer Duty evidence), and optionally CAP-001 (Retail Banking — if cash balances or mortgage offset positions are discussed in the holistic review).

phases.name: Review Scheduling and Pre-Meeting Preparation
phases.description: The Wealth Advisor schedules the annual suitability review meeting, retrieves and assembles the client's current portfolio position, recent performance data, suitability record from the prior review, and any material change flags (life event triggers, risk score drift alerts, ESG preference updates). The system pre-populates a review pack for the advisor.
governance_rules: GOV-007-R03 — Consumer Duty ongoing service evidence
entry_conditions: Client relationship is active with a discretionary or advisory mandate
Annual review date has been reached OR a material change trigger has fired (life event, risk score drift, ESG update)
exit_conditions: Review meeting scheduled and confirmed
Pre-meeting pack assembled: portfolio snapshot, performance summary, prior suitability record, and change-of-circumstances questionnaire sent to client

phases.name: Client Risk Profile and Objectives Reassessment
phases.description: During the review meeting, the Wealth Advisor walks the client through an updated suitability questionnaire to reassess financial situation, investment objectives, risk tolerance, investment knowledge, and sustainability preferences. Any material changes are recorded. The system scores the questionnaire and produces an updated risk profile. If the risk profile has changed, the system flags portfolio suitability gaps versus the current mandate.
governance_rules: GOV-007-R03 — Consumer Duty fair value outcome evidence
entry_conditions: Pre-meeting pack has been reviewed by advisor
exit_conditions: Updated suitability questionnaire responses recorded
Updated risk profile score produced and agreed with client
Sustainability preference record updated
Material change flags resolved or escalated

phases.name: Portfolio Performance Review and Rebalancing Recommendation
phases.description: The Wealth Advisor presents the portfolio's performance against the agreed benchmark (ARC/WMA index), attribution analysis, and costs-and-charges ex-post disclosure (MiFID II COBS 9A). Based on the reassessed risk profile and current portfolio allocation, the system generates a draft rebalancing recommendation. The advisor reviews, adjusts, and finalises the recommendation. If cross-capability data is needed (e.g. cash savings account balance for liquidity buffer, or mortgage outstanding for net worth), it is retrieved via an async event request.
governance_rules: GOV-007-R01 — recommendation must be based on updated suitability record
GOV-007-R03 — ex-post costs and charges disclosure
entry_conditions: Updated risk profile has been confirmed (PH-072 complete)
exit_conditions: Performance review presented to client
Ex-post costs and charges disclosed to client
Rebalancing recommendation finalised by advisor
Client has reviewed and is ready to give instructions

phases.name: Client Instructions and Suitability Report Issuance
phases.description: The client gives formal instructions to proceed with the rebalancing (or declines). The system generates a MiFID II-compliant suitability report documenting the basis for each recommendation, the client's updated circumstances, and the charges applicable. The suitability report is provided to the client before any trade execution. The advisor countersigns. A cross-capability event is published to CAP-005 (Compliance) to register the suitability record in the central compliance audit trail.
governance_rules: GOV-007-R01 — suitability report must be issued before execution
GOV-007-R03 — Consumer Duty fair value documentation
FCA COBS 9A.3.2 — written suitability report required
entry_conditions: Rebalancing recommendation has been presented to client (PH-073 complete)
Client has read and acknowledged the suitability report
exit_conditions: Client instructions recorded (proceed or decline)
Suitability report issued and acknowledged by client
Suitability record published to CAP-005 compliance audit trail
Ex-ante costs and charges disclosure provided

phases.name: Rebalancing Trade Execution
phases.description: Following client approval, the Wealth Platform Service instructs the custody platform (FNZ/SEI) to execute the approved rebalancing trades: sell overweight positions, buy underweight instruments, and reinvest cash. MiFID II best execution obligations apply. Trade confirmations are received and matched to the order records. The portfolio allocation is updated to reflect post-rebalancing positions.
governance_rules: GOV-007-R01 — execution only after suitability report issued
FCA PROD target market check before each instrument purchase
entry_conditions: Client instructions to proceed received (PH-074 complete)
Ex-ante costs and charges disclosure provided
exit_conditions: All approved rebalancing trades executed via custody platform
Trade confirmations received and matched
Portfolio allocation updated
Post-trade portfolio snapshot stored

phases.name: Post-Review Reporting and Consumer Duty Evidence
phases.description: The system generates the final post-review report including updated portfolio valuation, transaction confirmations, updated asset allocation chart, and a Consumer Duty fair value evidence record. The annual suitability report is stored in the compliance system with a minimum 5-year retention period. The next review date is set. A cross-capability event signals to CAP-005 that the Consumer Duty fair value evidence record has been completed.
governance_rules: GOV-007-R03 — Consumer Duty annual service evidence
entry_conditions: Trade execution confirmed (PH-075 complete) or client declined rebalancing (PH-074 exit: decline path)
exit_conditions: Post-review client report dispatched
Suitability record archived in compliance system (5-year WORM retention)
Consumer Duty fair value evidence record completed
Next review date set on portfolio record
Journey marked complete

happy_path.description: Wealth Advisor schedules and conducts the annual review. Client's risk profile is unchanged or has minor updates. Rebalancing recommendation is agreed. Suitability report issued. Trades executed successfully. Post-review reporting completed. All MiFID II and Consumer Duty obligations discharged.

alternative_paths.name: Client Declines Rebalancing
alternative_paths.description: The client reviews the rebalancing recommendation in PH-073 or PH-074 and declines to proceed with some or all proposed trades. The advisor documents the client's decision and the basis for it. The suitability report is still issued, noting the client's instruction to deviate from the recommendation. Post-review reporting documents the unchanged portfolio and the client's stated rationale.
alternative_paths.notes: COBS 9A requires that the suitability report document any client instruction that diverges from the advisor's recommendation. Consumer Duty evidence record must capture the client's informed decision.

alternative_paths.name: Cash Balance Discussion — Retail Banking Cross-Capability View
alternative_paths.description: During PH-073, the Wealth Advisor and client agree they need to review the client's cash holdings on the retail banking side (e.g. savings account balance for liquidity buffer assessment, or mortgage outstanding for net wealth calculation). SVC-016 publishes an async event to request account data from CAP-001. Once received, the holistic wealth view is incorporated into the rebalancing recommendation before proceeding to PH-074.
alternative_paths.notes: Cross-capability data access from CAP-006 to CAP-001 is exclusively via async event on the Event Bus. SVC-016 never calls SVC-001 directly.

alternative_paths.name: Risk Profile Material Change — Mandate Reassessment Required
alternative_paths.description: During PH-072, the client's updated questionnaire reveals a material change in circumstances (e.g. retirement, significant windfall, divorce). The updated risk profile results in a significant mismatch with the current investment mandate. The Wealth Advisor refers the case to the Head of Suitability before issuing any recommendation. Following sign-off, the mandate is formally amended and a new suitability report issued.
alternative_paths.notes: GOV-007-R01 approval chain: Wealth Advisor → Head of Suitability for complex cases. Mandate amendment requires a new client agreement in addition to the suitability report.

exception_paths.name: Suitability Record Incomplete — Cannot Proceed to Execution
exception_paths.description: At PH-074, the suitability report generation fails validation (e.g. mandatory fields missing, questionnaire responses incomplete, Head of Suitability sign-off not obtained for a referred case). Trade execution (PH-075) is blocked until the suitability record is complete and signed. The compliance system raises an exception alert. COBS 9A prohibits issuing a recommendation without a complete suitability record.
exception_paths.resolution: Advisor completes missing information. Head of Suitability signs off. Suitability report regenerated and issued. Journey resumes at PH-074 exit.
exception_paths.governance_impact: GOV-007-R01 constraint: no investment recommendation without a current and documented suitability record.

exception_paths.name: Custody Platform Trade Execution Failure
exception_paths.description: During PH-075, one or more rebalancing trades fail at the custody platform (FNZ/SEI) due to a settlement failure, instrument suspension, or market halt. The partial execution state is recorded. The advisor is notified. Unfilled orders are either retried or cancelled. The post-review report documents the partial execution and the remaining open orders.
exception_paths.resolution: Failed trades are retried on next settlement cycle or cancelled with advisor approval. Post-review report updated to reflect final execution state.
exception_paths.governance_impact: MiFID II best execution obligation: failed orders must be documented with the reason for failure.

exception_paths.name: Client Unreachable — Review Overdue
exception_paths.description: The client does not respond to scheduling communications for the annual review. After 3 contact attempts within 30 days, the case is escalated to the Head of Wealth Management. The overdue review is recorded in the compliance system. Consumer Duty requires that ongoing fees are only charged where ongoing service is demonstrably delivered — the overdue review is a potential Consumer Duty breach if the advisory charge is continued.
exception_paths.resolution: Escalation to Head of Wealth Management. Client may be placed on a fee suspension or relationship review. If unreachable for 6+ months, the account enters a closed-book review process.
exception_paths.governance_impact: GOV-007-R03 Consumer Duty constraint: ongoing advisory charges may only be levied where ongoing service is demonstrably delivered.

design_decisions.decision: The Wealth Platform Service (SVC-016, CAP-006) is the sole owner of all review workflow entities. CAP-001 account data is accessed via async event only (ALT-002).
design_decisions.rationale: Cross-capability communication is exclusively async. SVC-016 must not call SVC-001 directly. The async event pattern ensures CAP-006 holds its own cached representation of client cash data, avoiding a hard runtime dependency on CAP-001 during the review meeting.

design_decisions.decision: The suitability report is published as a cross-capability event to CAP-005 (Compliance) for the central compliance audit trail. SVC-016 does not write directly to the CAP-005 database.
design_decisions.rationale: SVC-014 (KYC/AML, CAP-005) is the authoritative compliance record store. SVC-016 publishes SuitabilityReportIssued (EVT-103). SVC-014 consumes it to create a SuitabilityRecord in its own data store. This follows the architecture's async cross-capability pattern and ensures the compliance record is consistent even if SVC-016 experiences a failure.

design_decisions.decision: Custody platform (FNZ/SEI) is modelled as an external system called synchronously by SVC-016 within the CAP-006 boundary. It is not a separate capability.
design_decisions.rationale: Per CAP-006 build-vs-buy decision DD-002, custody is a buy candidate — FNZ or SEI. The custody platform is an external dependency within SVC-016's boundary, not a peer capability. SVC-016 wraps the custody API internally. This avoids introducing a spurious capability boundary for a vendor dependency.
